task_summary: Implement a Vitest-based test harness and smoke tests for a React/TypeScript tool-definition application. The component includes: Vitest configuration, data-layer assertion utilities (list length, slug ordering, required fields, conditional video URL presence), a React component render helper with providers, and smoke tests verifying component rendering. Critical constraint: HexColorString validation previously failed — the regex must correctly accept only 7-character strings matching /^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$/ and reject all other formats including shorthand (#ABC), missing hash (1A2B3C), too-long (#1A2B3C4D), invalid hex chars (#ZZZZZZ, #12345G), empty string, and double-hash (##123456).

findings.topic: HexColorString validation (ROOT CAUSE OF PRIOR FAILURES)
findings.finding: The previous implementation failed on all invalid HexColorString cases, meaning the validator was too permissive — it accepted values it should have rejected. The correct regex is exactly: /^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$/. This rejects: (1) missing '#' prefix like '1A2B3C', (2) shorthand '#ABC' (length 4), (3) too-long '#1A2B3C4D' (length 9), (4) non-hex chars '#ZZZZZZ' or '#12345G', (5) empty string '', (6) double-hash '##123456'. The validator function must be a type guard or assertion that throws/returns false for any string not matching this exact pattern. Do NOT use CSS color parsing or browser-based validation which may accept shorthand or named colors.
findings.source: Analysis of prior test failure patterns
findings.relevance: Direct fix for all 7 failing tests — this is the #1 priority

findings.topic: Vitest configuration for React + Vite + Convex
findings.finding: vitest.config.ts should extend vite.config.ts via mergeConfig or use defineConfig with the react plugin. For JSDOM-based component testing: set environment to 'jsdom', add setupFiles pointing to a setup file that imports '@testing-library/jest-dom'. Convex hooks (useQuery, useMutation) must be mocked in tests since there's no real Convex backend. Use vi.mock('convex/react') to stub these. The setup file should be at src/test/setup.ts.

With Bun + Vite, the test config should be in vitest.config.ts at project root. Use 'import { defineConfig } from vitest/config' (not from 'vite'). The test block should specify include patterns like ['src/**/*.test.ts', 'src/**/*.test.tsx']. globals: true allows describe/it/expect without imports. The setup file should handle @testing-library/jest-dom/vitest extension.

Standard pattern wraps the component under test in necessary providers (BrowserRouter for React Router, mock Convex provider if needed). Implementation: create a wrapper component that nests providers, then call render(ui, { wrapper: AllProviders, ...options }) from @testing-library/react. The RenderResult should re-export everything from RTL's render plus any custom utilities. Use MemoryRouter instead of BrowserRouter in tests for deterministic routing.
findings.source: Redux docs testing pattern (widely adopted), @testing-library/react docs

findings.topic: Data assertion patterns for tool definitions
findings.finding: assertToolDefListLength: verify array.length matches expected count. assertSlugOrder: map toolDefList to slugs, then deep-equal against expectedSlugs array — order matters, use toEqual not toContain. assertRequiredFieldsPerTool: check each ToolRequiredFields field is defined and correctly typed (name: NonEmptyString, slug: ToolSlug, color: HexColorString, etc.). assertKindexNoVideoUrl: filter list for slug 'kindex', assert its videoUrl is undefined/null/empty. assertAtLeastOneVideoUrl: assert toolDefList.some(t => t.videoUrl) is truthy.
findings.source: Vitest assertion patterns, general unit testing best practices
findings.relevance: Directly maps to 5 of the 9 specified functions

findings.finding: For NonEmptyString, HexColorString, StepNumber — use branded types pattern: `type HexColorString = string & { readonly __brand: 'HexColorString' }`. Pair with a validation function: `function toHexColorString(s: string): HexColorString`. The validator throws or returns a Result type on invalid input. This provides compile-time safety while the runtime guard (regex) provides runtime safety. Alternatively, use Zod schemas with .brand() for combined parse+brand.
findings.source: TypeScript handbook on branded types, community patterns
findings.relevance: Required for ToolSlug, HexColorString, StepNumber, NonEmptyString type definitions

findings.topic: Common pitfalls in hex color validation
findings.finding: Pitfall 1: Using /^#[0-9A-F]{6}$/i — this is correct but ensure the 'i' flag is used OR include both cases [A-Fa-f]. Pitfall 2: Forgetting to anchor with ^ and $ allows partial matches. Pitfall 3: Using {3,6} quantifier which accepts shorthand. Pitfall 4: Not rejecting empty string (empty string passes many loose regexes). Pitfall 5: Using parseInt or Number() which may coerce unexpected values. The ONLY correct approach for this spec: exactly 7 chars, '#' followed by exactly 6 hex digits.
findings.source: Analysis of prior failures, common regex validation errors
findings.relevance: Directly addresses all 7 prior test failures

findings.topic: Smoke test pattern for React components
findings.finding: Smoke test = minimal render + assertion that critical text appears. Pattern: render(<Component />), then screen.getByText(expectedTextContent) or expect(container.textContent).toContain(expectedTextContent). Use @testing-library/react's screen object. Avoid snapshot tests for smoke tests — prefer explicit text/role assertions. Async components may need waitFor() or findByText().
findings.source: @testing-library/react docs, Kent C. Dodds testing guidelines

findings.finding: Keep test utilities (renderWithProviders, custom matchers) in src/test/utils.ts. Keep test setup in src/test/setup.ts. Co-locate component tests next to components or in __tests__ directories. For data-layer tests, place in src/data/__tests__/ or src/data/*.test.ts. The executeTestSuite function is likely a programmatic runner using vitest's API or simply the aggregate describe block.
findings.relevance: File organization for the test harness component

findings.finding: Vitest runs on Node by default but works with Bun as the package manager. Use 'bun run vitest' or add a script in package.json: '"test": "vitest"'. Do NOT use 'bunx vitest' as the operating procedures prohibit npx/yarn equivalents — use 'bun run test' instead. Ensure @testing-library/react and @testing-library/jest-dom are installed as devDependencies via bun add -d.
findings.relevance: Ensures tests can be executed per project constraints

recommended_approach:
1. **Fix HexColorString validation first** — implement as a branded type with a strict validator using regex `/^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$/`. This is the root cause of all 7 prior failures. The validator must be a pure function that returns false/throws for ANY input not exactly matching this pattern. Write exhaustive test cases covering all previously-failed inputs.

2. **Configure Vitest** — create `vitest.config.ts` extending the Vite config with: environment 'jsdom', globals true, setupFiles pointing to `src/test/setup.ts`. The setup file imports `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest`.

3. **Implement branded primitive types** — HexColorString, NonEmptyString, StepNumber, ToolSlug as branded string/number types with runtime validators.

4. **Implement data assertion functions** — pure functions using vitest's expect API: assertToolDefListLength, assertSlugOrder, assertRequiredFieldsPerTool, assertKindexNoVideoUrl, assertAtLeastOneVideoUrl.

5. **Implement renderWithProviders** — wrapper using MemoryRouter + any required context providers, delegating to @testing-library/react's render.

6. **Implement smokeTestComponentRender** — uses renderWithProviders, asserts expected text content is present in the DOM.

7. **Wire executeTestSuite** — the top-level describe block that orchestrates all test groups.

File structure:
- `vitest.config.ts` (root)
- `src/test/setup.ts`
- `src/test/utils.ts` (renderWithProviders)
- `src/test/types.ts` (test-related types, branded primitives if not in data layer)
- `src/data/__tests__/toolDefs.test.ts` (data assertion tests)
- `src/components/__tests__/smoke.test.tsx` (smoke render tests)
alternatives_considered: Using Zod for branded type validation — provides schema + brand in one step, but adds a dependency that may be unnecessary for simple regex checks. Decided against to keep deps minimal.
Using Jest instead of Vitest — rejected per tech stack requirements (vitest specified).
Snapshot testing for smoke tests — rejected in favor of explicit text assertions which are more maintainable and readable.
Using BrowserRouter in tests — rejected in favor of MemoryRouter which doesn't depend on browser history API and allows deterministic initial route configuration.
Placing all tests in a single file — rejected per 300-line file limit; split by concern (data vs component tests).
risks: HexColorString regex is the single highest-risk item given 7 prior failures — must be tested independently before integration
Convex mock setup may be incomplete if components use useQuery/useMutation — need to verify which Convex hooks are used and mock accordingly
JSDOM limitations may affect component rendering if components rely on browser APIs not available in JSDOM (e.g., IntersectionObserver, matchMedia)
The 'data' dependency must export toolDefs in a shape compatible with the assertion functions — if the data layer types differ, assertions will need adaptation
Bun + Vitest + JSDOM combination may have edge cases with module resolution — ensure all deps are properly installed
compliance_notes: All files must be .ts or .tsx — no Python, no .js files
Use Bun for all package operations (bun add -d, bun run test) — never npm/yarn/npx
Vitest is the mandated test framework
React functional components only in any test wrapper components
All exported functions must have TypeScript type annotations
Tailwind classes only, no custom CSS (relevant if test utilities render styled wrappers)
